_doc: Bounds on what the scheduled reconcile is allowed to re-ship. Read by 1_cicd/src/scripts/cloud-ship-reconcile-reship.sh. These are the operator's safety knobs for #354 and they live here, not inside the script, so raising or lowering the fleet's auto-repair aggression is a data edit.
_doc_reship_classes: Which cloud-ship-reconcile.sh finding classes get automatically re-shipped. `drift` (running digest != registry digest) is the #354 signature and is always safe to re-ship: the deploy is idempotent and the service was ALREADY meant to be at that digest. `absent` and `unpublished` are deliberately excluded — nine services read absent on the fleet for reasons that are not #354 (retired, on-demand, run outside compose), and auto-shipping them would hold the single WG runner to fix nothing. They are reported for a human instead. `created` (#560) IS re-shipped: a declared container that exists but never started is a deploy that was cut short — the same #354 mechanism — and the deploy's down+up is exactly the repair. `stopped` (exited/dead/paused, not a declared one_shot) is NOT: a crashed long-runner is not fixed by re-deploying the same image, and re-shipping it every run would hold the WG lock to fix nothing.
_doc_max_reships_per_run: Hard cap on services dispatched by ONE reconcile run. The re-ship runs on ship-wg-runner, the fleet's single deploy lock, and #179 is the standing reminder of what a long hold on that lock costs: cgc-db index jobs held it for up to 5.5 hours and every deploy behind them was evicted. An uncapped reconcile finding 40 drifted services would reproduce exactly that outage while believing it was repairing one. 5 services is roughly 15-50 minutes of lock, inside the deploy job's 90-minute ceiling with room to spare. The remainder is NOT lost: it is reported, and the next scheduled reconcile picks it up, because a reconcile converges by repetition rather than by finishing in one pass.

absent_redeploy._doc: Bounds for 1_cicd/src/scripts/cloud-ship-reconcile-absent-redeploy.sh, run by the reconcile job after the re-ship. `absent` (declared, no container at all) is still NOT re-shipped — reship_classes above is unchanged. Instead, for absent findings ONLY, at most ONE service per reconcile run gets `docker compose up -d --no-recreate --no-build --pull never` on the project the last Ship left on its VM: no rsync, no pull, no down, no eviction. Never while a cgc-db restore runs or is queued (GitHub and the VM are both checked, and "cannot tell" counts as "running"). Skipped and alerted when the VM has no engine-deployed project, an image is not cached, or another container holds the service's .ports.app. Why: matomo-hybrid was evicted on 2026-10-10 by a port-only socket match and the reconcile reported it absent for three days while one compose up would have repaired it (backlog #986).
absent_redeploy._doc_settle_seconds: How long after `up -d` the container states are read. Long enough for a container that dies on start (port clash, missing secret) to show as exited rather than running.

exclude.bc-obs_alerts-api: absent by design per cloud-ship-reconcile.sh (retired, on-demand or run outside compose)
exclude.infra-bld_gha-runner: absent by design per cloud-ship-reconcile.sh (on-demand self-hosted runner)
exclude.infra-obs_openobserve: absent by design per cloud-ship-reconcile.sh (retired, on-demand or run outside compose)
exclude.user-media_playlist-syncer: absent by design per cloud-ship-reconcile.sh; also declares ports.app 8090, which ntfy holds on oci-apps

absent_redeploy._doc_exclude: Service dirs the redeploy never touches, each with its reason. Seeded with the services cloud-ship-reconcile.sh already names as absent for reasons that are not an eviction and that are still absent on 2026-10-14. Removing an entry lets the reconcile start it again.

ntfy._doc: Best-effort alert for every redeploy, failure and safety skip, posted from `vm` over ssh (the same unauthenticated path cloud-health-mail-full.sh uses). NTFY_URL in the environment overrides `url`. A failed alert never fails the run; the GitHub annotation still carries it.
